previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of frequent hospitalizations for nausea, vomiting, and back pain was admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis due to uncontrolled hyperglycemia. She presented with high blood glucose of 595, an elevated anion gap, and dehydration. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved the acidosis. Her diet was advanced successfully, and her blood sugars stabilized. Imaging showed no acute abdominal process. Her insulin regimen was adjusted to 24 units of glargine at bedtime with a revised sliding scale. Acute kidney injury improved with hydration, and lisinopril was restarted. Social work facilitated outpatient mental health and medical follow-up to address ongoing challenges with adherence and anxiety. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and coordinated follow-up care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Gastroenteritis/Gastroparesis flare: Pt was recently discharged 
for similar symptoms and initially presented to the ED with LBP 
and was discharged with better pain control.  She returned that 
evening with nausea, vomiting and inability to take po.  Pt was 
treated with IVF, bowel rest, reglan and anti-emetics.  She was 
noted to have diarrhea but was unable to provide a sample for 
Cx.  She failed an initial attempt at po challenges and lost PIV 
access requiring IM medications.  PICC line was placed on ___ 
and she was aggressively hydrated on strict bowel rest.  Over 
the following 48hrs, the N/V/D resolved and she was slowly 
advanced a diabetic diet without complications.   Pt was 
discharged on reglan 10mg TIDAC and zofran as needed.
.
Type I DM: Pt is poorly controlled at baseline with Hgb A1c >10% 
but was no in DKA on presentation.  Blood sugars were covered 
with half dose lantus while NPO with sliding scale.  Pt was 
advanced a diabetic diet and lantus was increased to home 
regimen of 24units daily with sliding scale humalog.  Pt is 
scheduled to follow up with ___.
. 
Acute Renal Failure: Pt presented with mild dehydration and 
continued to have vomiting/diarrhea with ongoing volume loss.  
Peripheral access was lost and pt became progressively 
dehydrated with mild tachycardia. On ___, a right PICC line was 
placed and pt was aggressively rehydrated. Her creatinine came 
down to 1.2 by the time of discharge.  Pt was instructed to get 
follow up labs on ___ during her PCP follow up appointment.
.
Anxiety/Social: Pt has a long standing history of anxiety and 
difficulty coping with her chronic illnesses.  She was very 
tearful, rolling around on the bed and alternatively sleeping 
under covers and refusing to interact with staff.   In addition, 
pt was noted to be having voluntary bowel incontinence and 
displaying regressive behavior.  Physical exam was notable for 
normal rectal tone and pt being able to tell you that she felt 
urgency but not wanting to get up to walk to the bathroom. 
Psychiatry was consulted, felt that this was behavioral.  A 
family meeting was held with the primary nurse, ___, SW, 
patient and MD where we discussed her anxiety/depression and 
suggested that this may be contributing to her readmissions and 
recurrent medical issues including gastroparesis.  Pt was 
minimally interactive during the meeting but behavior improved 
significantly over the next 2 days.  Pt was back to baseline and 
asking to return home by the day of discharge.   She will be 
seeing her PCP ___ ___ and HCA SW is working to find her a new 
counselor as this supportive relationship was effective for her 
in the past.  In addition, we discussed the idea of restarting 
an SSRI as an outpatient to help manage her chronic anxiety.  
.
UTI: Urine Cx was positive for coag negative staph.  Pt was 
treated empirically with Cipro and transitioned to Macrobid to 
complete the course.
.
Hypertension: Pt was notably hypertensive during admission and 
IV metoprolol was used while she was NPO.  After she was 
tolerating po diet, lisinopril was restarted and increased to 
20mg daily.  BP was much better controlled on this regimen and 
pt was given a prescription to continue this increased dose.
